title: HDD Inspector
description:
You must be able to work in the U.S. without sponsorship. No C2C or 3rd parties, please.

HDD (Horizontal Directional Drilling) Inspector in Danville, VA area (for projects located in North Carolina and Virginia)

  • $1,200–$1,350/day plus expenses
  • Contract role, on-site
  • Daily travel between project sites required

We're seeking an experienced HDD (Horizontal Directional Drilling) Inspector to serve as the owner's representative during pipeline construction activities across two project sites located approximately 20 miles apart in North Carolina and Virginia. This role is critical to ensuring drilling operations are executed safely, efficiently, and in compliance with engineering designs, environmental requirements, and project standards.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Monitor HDD contractors throughout all phases of drilling operations to ensure compliance with approved plans and specifications
  • Enforce OSHA regulations and project-specific safety requirements while promoting a strong safety culture in the field
  • Participate in daily Job Safety Analysis (JSA) meetings and safety discussions
  • Track drilling performance metrics, including rates of penetration, steering corrections, drilling fluid properties, and equipment conditions
  • Review and verify adherence to approved bore paths and engineering designs
  • Complete and maintain HDD inspection reports, drilling fluid logs, steering logs, and daily construction documentation
  • Identify and communicate potential environmental, safety, or operational concerns before they impact project execution
  • Serve as the primary liaison between the construction management team and drilling contractors
  • Monitor contractor performance and ensure compliance with project quality standards and regulatory requirements
  • Support successful project execution through proactive communication and issue resolution

Required Qualifications:

  • API 1169 Pipeline Construction Inspector certification
  • Previous experience inspecting HDD operations, pipeline construction, or midstream infrastructure projects
  • Strong understanding of drilling operations, bore path monitoring, and drilling fluid management
  • Experience working in active construction environments with multiple stakeholders
  • Knowledge of OSHA regulations, environmental compliance requirements, and pipeline construction standards
  • Strong documentation, reporting, and communication skills
  • Ability to work independently in a field-based environment while managing multiple priorities

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience supporting natural gas transmission, gathering, or midstream pipeline projects
  • Prior experience serving as an owner's representative or third-party inspector
  • Familiarity with utility crossings, environmental compliance monitoring, and construction quality assurance processes
  • Strong working knowledge of HDD steering systems, drilling fluid programs, and construction best practices

What We Offer:

  • Competitive daily rate
  • Expenses reimbursed
  • Opportunity to support critical pipeline infrastructure projects
  • High-visibility role with significant field responsibility and stakeholder interaction

If you have a strong background in HDD inspection, pipeline construction, or midstream operations and are looking for a field leadership opportunity supporting critical infrastructure projects, we'd like to hear from you.

description:

We're seeking an experienced Site Quality Assurance (QA) Manager to lead all quality assurance and quality control activities for a major energy infrastructure construction project. This is a high-impact opportunity to play a critical role in ensuring construction quality, regulatory compliance, and project success from construction through commissioning and turnover.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Strong knowledge of construction quality standards, inspection processes, and quality management systems.
  • Experience leading multidisciplinary quality teams and managing third-party inspectors.
  • Ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications, codes, and standards.
  • Excellent leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Certified Quality Auditor (CQA) certification preferred.
  • ASQ certifications highly desirable.
  • Previous experience supporting combined cycle gas turbine (CCGT) projects preferred.
  • Prior experience working on Kiewit projects is a strong plus.
  • Experience supporting commissioning, startup, and turnover phases of major projects.
  • Familiarity with ISO 9001 quality management systems.

Work Environment:

  • Active construction site environment.
  • Occasional extended work hours may be required to support critical project milestones and outage schedules.

If you're a quality-focused leader with a strong background in power generation, industrial construction, or EPC projects and are looking to make an impact on a major energy project, we'd love to connect.

description:
Industrial Construction Estimator
Contract Role
Ann Arbor, MI OR Pittsburgh, PA OR Charlotte, NC
Minimal travel required 5% - 15%
$55.00 - $75.00 per hour + benefits including
Medical, Dental, Vision, Paid Holidays, Accrued PTO, 401k with company match after 90 days.

Description

  • Coordinate full estimating service efforts for all Construction Specification Institute (CSI) divisions on large, complex work within Lump Sum, Design Build and Construction Management contractual formats.
  • Interpret designs, drawings, specifications, and other contract documents
  • Operate across multiple delivery systems or be very proficient in one specific type of system. Coordinate with cross-functional teams and stakeholders.
  • Manage the budget, conduct financial forecasting, and resource allocation. Identify, assess, and mitigate project risks.
  • Thrive in fast-paced, dynamic environments and adapt to changing project requirements.
 
Your Key Responsibilities
  • Proposal Reviews: Reviewing proposal specifications, drawings, attending pre-bid meetings to determine scope of work and required contents of estimate.
  • Scope Development: Developing and understanding scope requirements and issuing subcontracts for heavy industrial "supporting” trades, such as boilermaker, steel, concrete, piping, and electrical work. Writing proper scopes of work during the bidding phase and upon award, engage in subcontractor proposal review meetings, with ultimate responsibility of final evaluation and negotiation of subcontracts.
  • Cost Preparation: Preparing cost estimate and bid documents for construction projects or services that are used by management in preparation of the bidding process. Ensuring accuracy and completeness of estimate and proposals.
  • Strategic Planning: Identifying competitive edge strategies and follow through to project award. Also identifying, reviewing, and communicating contractual requirements such as risk factors, schedule, insurance, bonding, and penalties with supervisors and developing an action plan for the estimate and project construction.
 
Required Qualifications
  • A bachelor's degree in engineering, architecture, construction management or related program is preferred, or equivalent professional training and experience with high school diploma.
  • 5+ years of estimating, preconstruction or related general construction management experience.
  • Proficiency in computer estimating applications (Excel, Estimating Software).
  • Experience using Microsoft Project or Primavera.
  • Verbal and written communication skills.
  • Organizational skills
